text: The purpose of this report is to introduce the Little Jamaica Initiative, a multifaceted response to 26 City Council recommendations resulting from six Member's motions and provide a status update. Approximately 50 years ago, the area along Eglinton Avenue West, also known as Little Jamaica, became an immigration settlement neighbourhood for newcomers from Jamaica and other Caribbean islands, and continues to serve as a distinct ethnic and cultural hub. The area is recognized for the clusters of Black-owned and operated businesses of cultural relevance and is internationally known for its contribution to the reggae genre of music. Similar to many neighbourhoods in Toronto, the area has enjoyed settlement from other newcomers, and has a rich Indigenous history closely connected to the numerous ravines and water tributaries that traverse through it.
